audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Swain four stages (Skill, Swain, Swain, Skill, Skill, Swain, Swain) on a lane Lucian wins at 57.14%, and it contradicted every why on the same page — whys[1] calls Level 2 'your single biggest window', whys[2] 'full lane control', whys[3] 'you out-trade his Q poke', whys[5] 'your first-item DPS still beats' him.
audit.why: The packet chart (Lucian, Lucian, Lucian, Lucian, Skill, Lucian, Swain) matches the prose line for line: Lucian owns 1 through 5, Level 6 is genuinely even because Demonic Ascension turns on, and 2+ items belongs to the drain-tank.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Lucian / Lucian / Lucian / Lucian / Skill / Lucian / Swain in both layers; diff EVEN -> FAVOURED with the matching tone and difficulty prose.

audit.why: Four spikes present and correctly owned against the corrected chart: Lvl 2 Lucian burst, Lvl 3 weave control, Lvl 6 Demonic Ascension, 2+ items Rylai/Liandry drain-tank.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove is called 'his E pull' six times and nothing says how it actually roots.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The root is on the RETURN pass — sidestepping the outbound wave and then standing still is the single most common way a Lucian dies in this lane, and the page currently tells him to dodge it as if it were a one-way skillshot. 850 range, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s.
audit.corrected: Return-trip mechanic written into report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns and phases[3].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two more interactions never appear anywhere: Death's Hand stacks per bolt, and Vision of Empire feeds him a Soul Fragment off you.
audit.why: Q text: 'Swain unleashes several bolts of eldritch power that pierce through enemies. Enemies hit take more damage for each bolt they are struck by' — so standing close, or hugging the wave, multiplies his poke; standing wide takes one bolt. W text: 'Champions hit are revealed and also grant Swain a Soul Fragment' — eating his W literally pays for the permanent max health and healing in Ravenous Flock. Both change how you stand in lane and neither was stated.
audit.corrected: Q bolt-stacking into dosFull[0].d, the W Soul Fragment into dosFull[2].d, the permanent-HP consequence into phases[6].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns tracked only Demonic Ascension and gave no numbers.
audit.why: R is 120s flat and, per Riot's text, is 'indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions' — so it does not have a fixed duration you wait out, you end it by leaving the 650 radius. The cooldown that actually governs your step-ups in lane is Nevermove at 12s, not the ult.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block re-pointed at Nevermove with numbers, plus the leave-the-radius rule; phases[4].why now carries the same point.

edits.before: Keep the pressure rolling but track Demonic Ascension — your lead is HP-bar bullying, not all-in math, until items arrive.
edits.after: Keep bullying, but track Nevermove: 12s at rank 1, and it roots on the way back to him, not on the way out to you.

edits.before: The Culling adds lane-clear and execute chip — use it through walls on recalls and low-HP escapes.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension lasts as long as he drains a champion — leave the 650 radius and it ends itself.

edits.before: You fall off relative to top-lane scalers — convert the lead into towers and roams before the 3-item brawlers arrive.
edits.after: Soul Fragments give him permanent max health and healing — a drain-tank you cannot burst. Cash the lead before this.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E dash has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Swain Nevermove: 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s — the wave roots on its RETURN, so sidestepping the outbound half is not enough. Demonic Ascension is 120s and ends the moment nobody is inside the 650 drain. - Your E dash has one job: the moment it all goes wrong.

edits.before: His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Death's Hand stacks damage per bolt that hits you — stand wide of the wave so one lands, not three.

edits.before: Swain whiffs Demonic Ascension and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Vision of Empire hands him a Soul Fragment when it hits you — dodge it.

edits.before: Track Swain’s Demonic Ascension: His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the return trip, not the outbound one — step out of the line, then step out again as it flies back to him.

notes: The packet defect 'never names any of Swain's abilities' was true of the full layer only — the content layer already describes the kit accurately (it just says 'his E pull' rather than Nevermove). Full now names Nevermove, Death's Hand, Vision of Empire, Demonic Ascension and Soul Fragments. report[8].t already carried 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain', which covers the flagged needs-antiheal interaction, so I spent the edit budget on the E return-root instead. Vision of Empire's range is 5500-7500 by rank — it is a map-wide pick tool, not a lane-poke tool, and I did not write it up as lane poke.
